title: Space begins about 100 km up, roughly an hour’s drive away
body: There is no sharp edge where the atmosphere ends; the air just thins out gradually. So the boundary of space is a convention. The FAI, which keeps aviation and spaceflight records, uses 100 km, the Kármán line, while US agencies have long awarded astronaut wings above 50 miles, about 80 km. The idea behind it: around those heights, the air is so thin that a wing would need roughly orbital speed to produce enough lift.

slides.heading: How high is space?

options: A wing would need orbital speed for lift
